The module comment and implementation disagree exactly where this entry says: TradingGit pending ids are an in-memory commit scan (order-sync-poller.ts:1-18; TradingGit.ts:692-748), while slow external listing precedes the pending guard. The target therefore separates external, known-order, and unknown-reconciliation jobs, keeps public jobs scope-free, and explicitly labels the small lifecycle variants as local scheduler ADTs rather than a universal SDK, ActionContractMap, or closed order taxonomy. Git remains a rebuildable audit projection only.

The target repairs this at the order-observation configuration boundary with PositiveDuration/Disabled, finite safe-integer milliseconds, no jitter, one fixed-delay due, typed events, and explicit provider budget admission; invalid input is rejected rather than silently defaulted, and this policy is not imposed on public data leaves.

The source captures a live UTA iterable plus process-local running/tickCount and fire-and-forget broker connect (order-sync-poller.ts:39-51; main.ts:104-128; UnifiedTradingAccount.ts:141-222). The target moves authority to startup recovery, durable jobs/checkpoints, declared provider layers, and a retained root scheduler handle; account reach, keyless, funded readOnly observation, public-data availability, and transaction admission are distinct facts. The source's running guard, tickCount modulo/first-tick behavior, and clearInterval-only stop are explicit (order-sync-poller.ts:53-61,98-104); the separate snapshot scheduler confirms polling needs owned lifecycle rather than another timer authority. The target permits coalescing only an unclaimed same-scope/schedule observation wake, returns explicit Deferred/Rejected outcomes, performs calls after a committed lease claim with epoch/CAS fencing, and never shares lossy telemetry policy with durable order work. Adapter rate-limit, coalescing-window, and heartbeat evidence remain empirical as required by the retained question.

The source slow lane skips keyless/unhealthy accounts and catches listing errors, while UTA returns zero when getOpenOrders is absent and the legacy IBroker contract permits unsupported empty arrays (order-sync-poller.ts:62-75; UnifiedTradingAccount.ts:964-980; broker.ts:577-584). The target correctly makes listing a provider-declared leaf, keeps structural absence out of the capability tree, and distinguishes Complete/Partial/Unavailable so only scope-complete evidence can produce NoNewOrders; no per-order guess or market-data fallback fills unknown external discovery. The adapter namespace/pagination/scope question remains retained.

The source-specific cost model is preserved: Git reconstructs pending parent/bracket ids and lookup hints (TradingGit.ts:692-748), listing-present orders avoid per-order calls, absent orders require confirmation, and no-listing accounts use in-memory age backoff (UnifiedTradingAccount.ts:844-915). The repaired target carries provider lookup/child/local-alias evidence in OrderRef, journals source snapshot sequence/freshness, moves backoff to durable notBefore, and keeps observation separate from approval/compensation while linking recovery only for already-sent effects. Retention, symbol lookup, freshness, and stable execution identity remain Unknown/OperatorRequired rather than inferred from MockBroker.

The source has a detached void timer callback, clearInterval-only stop, no order-sync shutdown in main, and fire-and-forget connection startup (order-sync-poller.ts:93-104; main.ts:179-189; UnifiedTradingAccount.ts:211-222). The target preserves stop-after-no-new-claims while requiring ordered AdmissionClosing→WorkersDraining→JobsPersisted acknowledgement→WriterDrained→CapabilityLayersClosed→SchedulerClosed, late-epoch fencing, and Unknown/RecoveryCase after a crossed dispatch boundary. Ordinary data stream close never becomes transaction compensation, and provider-native close details remain unclaimed.
